mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday trip chaining into retail and recreation will keep weakening over the next four weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC lower than in the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise by at least 5 points for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 4-week mean, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in TRANSIT below its recent trough reduces spontaneous retail visits with a short lag, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next one to two weeks unless transit usage rebounds quickly.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 and remains there for 2 consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -20 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within the next 14 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM improves while PARKS remain deeply negative, discretionary shopping substitutes toward necessity trips and away from retail leisure, causing RETAIL_REC to trend lower over the following four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while PARKS stay below -20 and RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 4 weeks, reject the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drop by more than 5 points week-on-week, retail demand weakens with a one-week lag because commuting and lunchtime shopping shrink immediately after the work-activity shock.
failure_condition: If a week-on-week WORKPLACES drop larger than 5 points is followed by no decline in RETAIL_REC within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL time combined with weak TRANSIT suppresses out-of-home retail trips; the effect should persist for two to four weeks because habit formation keeps people at home after mobility contracts.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +7 and TRANSIT remains below -15 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 4-week mean, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained uptick in PARKS mobility precedes retail outings through leisure spillovers: more outdoor activity creates additional incidental shopping on the same or next week, lifting RETAIL_REC over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from its recent weekly mean
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by 10 points or more and RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 14 days, reject the spillover claim.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES move in opposite directions, retail demand becomes split between necessity and commuting channels; if WORKPLACES continues to lag while GROCERY_PHARM softens, RETAIL_REC will fall over four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -20 and GROCERY_PHARM is near zero or negative for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the previous 4 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals reduced citywide circulation, and retail activity should decline further over the next month rather than stabilize.
failure_condition: If restrictions tighten but both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recover by at least 5 points and RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior 4-week mean, the mechanism fails.
